title: Arrival in the West; Detroit, small towns, and Canada
description: Corky and Roberta begin by discussing where they have lived, Corky's preference for the West and small towns, and an anxious family stop in Detroit. They then talk about Idaho, Montana, and the region's ties to Canada, with side comments on weather and travel.

title: Courtship, marriage, and train travel
description: The conversation turns to Corky's meeting and marriage to Ernie, followed by her first-class train trip to Iowa with a friend. She describes plans to keep their identities secret and the lightning and thunderstorms they feared.

title: Flapper days; bobbed hair and 1920s style
description: Corky talks about being a flapper in high school, begging to bob her hair, her sister Mays cutting it, and the clothes, glasses, makeup, and grooming routines that went with the style. She then recalls dance halls, Fourth of July celebrations, and Spokane entertainment.

title: Youth in the 1920s; education and advice
description: She reflects on what it was like to come of age in the 1920s, comparing it with the 1960s, and recalls her mother and grandmother's reactions to fashion. Roberta then describes her graduate studies, and Corky encourages her to pursue a master's degree locally.

title: First teaching job; Helmer and winter travel
description: Corky starts an account of her first school assignment in Helmer, describing how remote it was and how she traveled there by train and then by sled in winter. The section ends as she begins to explain the hardship of that teaching post.
